title: Python: a re-export hop reads the hop module's bindings after del or reassignment, and a comprehension target does not bind in the same-module path (DEC-303 (a49) item 5)
description: DEC-303 (a49) item 5, opum-ai/opum-doc#2016 (ODOC-640), 2026-11-26T11:43Z, verbatim: 'N3, a re-export hop that resolves n.f without reading n's bindings after del f or f = wrap(f), predates #183. It is the wrong-edge class: GCLI-116's own invariant, one hop further. It gets its own task, together with N1's same-module path, and lands before the freeze. It may share code with NB-b, in the leader's order.' Found by the #183 round 1 review. Parts: (1) N3: symbolInModuleOrReexport and the module-attribute re-export chain follow from n import f hops without reading n's module-level bindings of f, so n.py: from m import f / del f (or f = wrap(f)) still resolves from n import f; f() to m.f; the gate in resolveImportBinding and resolveModuleAttribute reads the bindings of the directly named module only. (2) N1 same-module path: a comprehension iteration target is recorded by the walker as a binding of the enclosing scope (comprehension: true) and the same-module bare-name path counts it, so a module-level def f plus _ = [0 for f in X] makes f rebound for a same-module call although Python binds the target in the comprehension's own scope (a walrus target inside a comprehension still binds the enclosing scope, PEP 572). Build: red/green fixtures with callee-symbol pinning and the full bin delta, positive twins, mutation checks by name, and the five-pin corpus diff per (a34) and (a40) item 2 with every in-repo edge created or removed reported before the clear. Lands before the analyzer freezes for the blind sample; joins the (a36) item 1(i) hold list (a49 item 7). Not built until the leader sends the GO.

acceptanceCriteria.text: n.py re-exporting f from m then del f or f = wrap(f): from n import f; f() and import n; n.f() resolve to no edge and are binned as a rebound name is; the twin without the del resolves to m.f, callee pinned, full bin delta

a same-module call to a def f with a comprehension target named f at module level resolves (the target is not a module binding); a walrus target inside a comprehension still makes f rebound; function-level behaviour unchanged
five-pin corpus diff script-asserted, each moved site named; any in-repo edge created or removed comes to opum-doc before the clear
mutation checks by name, each red
